sentences: This bill would create a special fund in the federal budget to pay the COVID-19 disaster payment to eligible workers.
It would set up a special appropriation that lets the government spend money as needed from the Consolidated Revenue Fund until 30 June 2022.
From 1 July 2021, the National Recovery and Resilience Agency would take over responsibility for the payment, and its annual report must include details of payments made.
changes: The bill establishes a special appropriation for the COVID-19 disaster payment.
It shifts responsibility for the payment to the National Recovery and Resilience Agency from 1 July 2021.
It requires the Coordinator-General of the National Recovery and Resilience Agency to include information about COVID-19 disaster payments in the agency's annual report.
summary.affected: Workers who are Australian citizens, permanent residents or temporary visa holders with work rights, aged 17 or over, who cannot earn their usual income due to public health restrictions in a COVID-19 hotspot and have liquid assets under $10,000.

Covid-19 Disaster Payment (Funding Arrangements) Bill 2021 - Second Reading - Quarantine and vaccine rollout

The majority voted against [requests for amendment](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22legislation%2Famend%2Fr6728_amend_bdf9dbcc-0c71-4aa3-93a8-96c47fc970c6%22;rec=0) that were proposed by the Greens Party, which means they failed. ### Amendment text > *(1) Clause 3, page 2 (line 18), at the end of the definition of COVID 19 disaster payment, add "as modified by section 3A of this Act".* > > *(2) Page 2 (after line 18), after Part 1, insert:* > >> *Part 1A — COVID 19 disaster payment* >> >> *3A COVID 19 disaster payment* >> >> *(1) The program for a COVID 19 disaster payment, as specified in item 492 of the table in Part 4 of Schedule 1AB to the Financial Framework (Supplementary Powers) Regulations 1997, must comply with the following requirements:* >> >>> *(a) the payments must be available under the program in respect of a location in Australia that is subject to a State or Territory public health order restricting the movement of persons for a period of 7 days or more;* >>> >>> *(b) the payments must be available in respect of the period starting on the first day the restrictions are imposed by the order (and not limited only to the period starting after the end of the 7 day period);* >>> >>> *(c) the availability of the payments in respect of the location must not be made subject to the Commonwealth Chief Medical Officer first determining the location to be a COVID 19 hotspot;* >>> >>> *(d) the eligibility criteria must not include requirements that a person:* >>> >>>> *(i) has less than $10,000 of liquid assets; or* >>>> >>>> *(ii) does not receive a Commonwealth income support payment or payment of a similar nature.* >> >> *(2) Subsection (1) applies notwithstanding item 492 of the table in Part 4 of Schedule 1AB to the Financial Framework (Supplementary Powers) Regulations 1997 and prevails to the extent of any inconsistency with that item.* >> >> *(3) The program for a COV

speeches.speaker: Andrew Giles
speeches.brief: Labor supported the COVID-19 Disaster Payment Bill but moved a second reading amendment criticising the government's failures in hotel quarantine, vaccine rollout, and income support, calling for dedicated quarantine facilities, improved vaccination efforts, a public information campaign, and domestic mRNA vaccine manufacturing.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the COVID-19 Disaster Payment Bill is needed solely because the Prime Minister failed on vaccine rollout and dedicated quarantine facilities. They claimed the budget assumes weekly lockdowns will continue, criticised the Treasurer for cutting JobKeeper (citing 56,000 job losses), and proposed a four-point plan: fix vaccinations, build quarantine facilities, launch a vaccine education campaign, and manufacture mRNA vaccines domestically.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: The COVID-19 Disaster Payment of $325 per week is insufficient, leaves workers without income for the first week, and excludes those with liquid assets over $10,000; the government should instead raise JobSeeker to $1,100 per fortnight and address insecure work, while the Morrison government’s quarantine failures caused the lockdown.

speeches.speaker: Kate Thwaites
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the COVID-19 Disaster Payment was welcome but came too late after the Morrison government was forced by Labor and Victoria to provide it, and that the vaccine rollout was botched, leaving many Victorians — including those who withdrew superannuation early — ineligible for the payment. They also criticised the government for failing to mount a public health education campaign, allowing misinformation such as Clive Palmer’s anti-vaccination pamphlets to circulate.

speeches.speaker: Susan Templeman
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the COVID-19 Disaster Payment bill is needed due to the Morrison government's failures in pandemic management, including inadequate quarantine facilities, a slow vaccine rollout (only 3% fully vaccinated), lack of information campaigns, and insufficient support for aged care and disability sectors. The speaker called for dedicated quarantine facilities, domestic mRNA vaccine production, and a clear forward plan.

speeches.speaker: Helen Haines
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the COVID-19 Disaster Payment bill but argued its eligibility rules unfairly exclude regional workers and businesses economically impacted by lockdowns in nearby cities like Melbourne, citing examples from the Indi electorate such as ski fields and hospitality venues. They called for the government to amend the framework to extend support to all workers suffering income loss due to the pandemic, not just those in designated hotspots.

speeches.speaker: Peta Murphy
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the COVID-19 Disaster Payment Bill but argued it was unnecessary, blaming the government for failing to roll out vaccines and establish fit-for-purpose quarantine facilities, citing 40,000 stranded Australians, 24 hotel quarantine leaks, and only 3% of the community fully vaccinated.

speeches.speaker: Josh Burns
speeches.brief: The government was shamed into introducing the COVID-19 Disaster Payment bill as a bare minimum after withdrawing earlier support and leaving Victoria stranded, and the vaccine rollout was criticised for relying too heavily on AstraZeneca, failing to procure enough Pfizer doses, and not using mass vaccination clinics or purpose-built quarantine facilities.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that ivermectin is an effective COVID-19 treatment and prophylaxis, citing studies showing a 62–67% reduction in death and 86% reduction in infections, and that 800,000 Australians received a vaccine later deemed risky by the Chief Medical Officer. He called for widespread adoption of ivermectin in Australia.

speeches.speaker: Scott Buchholz
speeches.brief: The COVID-19 Disaster Payment (Funding Arrangements) Bill 2021 appropriates funds from the Consolidated Revenue Fund to finance the COVID-19 disaster payment for the 2021-22 financial year.
